newsitem.title: USA: Klimt landscape brings $14.7 million in New York.
newsitem.headline: Klimt landscape brings $14.7 million in New York.

text.p: A landscape by Gustav Klimt, who is better known for his heavily decorated, often erotic female forms, set a new record on Tuesday night for the Austrian painter when it was auctioned for $14.7 million.
The sale, at Sotheby's, was for nearly three times the painting's estimate. The buyer was anonymous.

"Litzlbergerkeller am Attersee," a green-imbued, perfectly square, large canvas work, shows a tavern in the Alps where Klimt spent time. Only about one-quarter of Klimt's works are landscapes, and nearly all of those were painted in this region.
Alexander Apsis, director of Sotheby's impressionist and modern department in New York, said the price was so high because the painting was "so extremely rare."

The evening auction, the most significant portion of an impressionist and modern sale, fell within its estimated range of $76 million to $99 million, bringing a total of $81 million. Last year the spring evening sale at Sotheby's totalled $65 million.
A pastel drawing by Edgar Degas of dancing girls adjusting their dress straps, "Danseuses," sold for $11 million, a record for a Degas pastel.
"Jeanne Hebuterne Con Cappello," a muted portrait by Amedeo Modigliani of his mistress and subsequent wife, sold for $9.6 million.
